quick_skim.title: MetaRSI / RSI2: A Meta-Recursive Self-Improving System for Recursive Self-Improving Systems Themselves
quick_skim.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) lets a system improve the model-building machinery from its own failures, so every later model inherits the gain. Yet RSI has been validated almost exclusively on coding and formal benchmarks such as science QA and mathematics. This format bound limits RSI to improvement within a machine-checkable slice, not general capability where questions are open and correctness is settled by argument, replication, or measurement. We argue RSI must next operate across real, diverse scientific, engineering, and meta-scientific domains, not where formal evaluation is merely tractable. To that end we present MetaRSI-v1, where improvement is the scheduled composition of three typed operators over one unified paradigm. Data-RSI amplifies existing competence and marks its boundary; Harness-RSI edits a five-slot scaffold without touching weights; Model-RSI internalizes capability into parameters through bounded training. Sharing one loop kernel and artifact vocabulary, they make data, scaffold, and model changes composable rather than exclusive. A two-axis optimizer jointly decides operator order and each operator's proposal policy, while a meta-level policy revises the schedule across terms. We validate MetaRSI-v1 under the field's standard evaluations, on code and closed-form science, with no external teacher: the target model plays every role in its own loop. MetaRSI-v1 reframes self-improvement from a single-surface edit to a composition across the full model-production pipeline, opening two paths: a model route internalizing capability through training, and a harness route leaving weights untouched and thus extending self-improvement to any model reachable through an interface, with Data-RSI redefined as the shared substrate feeding both. The framework further yields refutable laws on where loops exist, how operators compose, and what supervision buys.

The authors present MetaRSI-v1, which schedules typed operators over a unified representation to extend self-improvement to open scientific and engineering domains.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 递归自我改进（RSI）能让系统从自身失败中改进建模机制，但其验证几乎局限于编码与形式化基准，难以覆盖开放性的科学问题。本文提出MetaRSI-v1，将改进过程建模为在统一表示上按计划组合三类带类型算子，使系统能够在真实多样的科学、工程与元科学领域中进行自我改进。该工作主张RSI应超越可机器检验的范围，为面向开放问题的自主研究系统提供了新范式。

quick_skim.title: AlphaRJM: Reward-Jump Memory for Stochastic Return-Guided Alpha Discovery
quick_skim.abstract: Formulaic alpha discovery is a pool-dependent symbolic search problem in which informative feedback is observed primarily when a complete expression is evaluated. This delayed feedback creates two coupled difficulties: the retained alpha pool does not preserve the full history of realized evaluation feedback, and the value of an intermediate construction action is uncertain because its consequence depends on the formula eventually completed. We introduce AlphaRJM, which addresses these difficulties through Reward-Jump Memory, an event-driven latent state that remains fixed during token construction and updates only at terminal evaluation events using the realized pool reward and evaluation outcome, and an action-conditioned SDE return critic that represents future discounted discovery returns with stochastic particles. The particles guide action selection through their mean and uncertainty and are learned using a distributional Bellman objective combining energy-distance matching, mean calibration, and jump regularization. Empirically, AlphaRJM delivers strong and stable gains across multiple equity universes, forecasting horizons, and random seeds, while ablations confirm the complementary roles of persistent evaluation history, stochastic return modeling, and distributional supervision.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: AlphaRJM addresses pool-dependent symbolic search for formulaic alpha discovery, using Reward-Jump Memory and an action-conditioned SDE return critic to handle delayed feedback.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 论文针对公式化Alpha发现这一池依赖符号搜索问题展开研究，其核心困难在于反馈仅在完整表达式被评估时才出现，导致中间构建动作的价值难以判断，且Alpha池无法保留完整评估反馈历史。作者提出AlphaRJM，引入奖励跳跃记忆作为事件驱动隐状态，在token构建阶段保持固定，仅在终端评估事件时依据实际池奖励与评估结果更新，并结合动作条件随机微分方程回报评论器进行信用分配。实验表明该机制能有效保留评估反馈、提升符号搜索效率。整体为延迟反馈下的符号表达式搜索提供了新的记忆与信用分配范式。
